newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 27.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sent a clear message that he is moving closer toward raising interest rates and also showed growing concern over stock prices. The Dow industrials dived more than 100 points on the remarks, but recovered to close at 6,983.18, down 55.03. Bond prices also fell, but the dollar rose.
* 3Com agreed to buy modem maker U.S. Robotics in a $6.6 billion stock deal that analysts called a bold challenge to market leader Cisco.
* CPC International said it would spin off its corn-refining business and focus on its packaged-food business, which includes Hellmann's mayonnaise and Skippy peanut butter.
* McDonald's plan to cut prices won't be followed by Wendy's or by Burger King, owned by Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc.
* The emergency board appointed to mediate a contract dispute between AMR's American Airlines and pilots begins hearings today.
* Japanese auto exports to the United States rose 75 percent in January.
* The mutual fund industry's trade group, the Investment Company Institute, has kept $1 million in a fund that has performed so poorly that Dean Witter is liquidating it.
* Sumitomo Corp Chairman Tomiichi Akiyama resigned, taking responsibility for the company's $2.6 billion copper trading scandal.
* February short interest on Nasdaq rose 2.9 percent to 1.36 billion shares.
* Philip Morris unveiled an $8 billion share repurchase program and a three-for-one stock split.
* Novell's fiscal first quarter earnings fell 20 percent, indicating that the company's turnaround is progressing more slowly than expected.
* Kodak extended chief executive George Fisher's employment contract by two years under revised terms that tie much of his potential compensation to stock options.
* Lucent shares fell 6.2 percent after a Smith Barney analyst criticized the company's accounting practices and sources of earnings, which Lucent defended.
* Will selling the wax dummies of Marilyn Monroe and Elvis make Pearson Plc a smarter stock play?
In an effort to return to its core business and boost its stock, the British publishing group is trying to find a buyer for its wax museum, Madame Tussaud's. -- Heard on the Street.

* Bond prices dropped yesterday, pushing interest rates to the highest level in nearly a month, after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said strength in the economy and in stocks may necessitate an increase in interest rates. -- Credit Markets.
